property_summary: After calling Collect, no address's balance can increase as a result.
After a call to Collect, the caller's balance cannot increase relative to its previous value.
After a Collect call, the change in the sum of all balances equals zero, i.e., the total token amount is conserved.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance is non-strictly decreasing (i.e., does not increase) when the call succeeds.
After Collect, the caller's balance never increases by more than the amount sent.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance cannot be less than MinSum if the call succeeded.
After any Collect call, the sum of all balances stays the same or decreases by exactly the amount collected (no increase).
If Collect succeeds, the caller's balance before the call is at least MinSum and strictly greater than the collected amount.
After any Collect call, the caller's balance is never exactly equal to the amount collected if it was at least MinSum before.
After any successful Collect call, the caller's balance change is exactly the amount collected (balances[caller] decreases by exactly _am).
After Collect, the caller's balance is non-negative and its change equals the withdrawn amount.
After a successful Collect call, the sum of all balances in the contract is preserved (increases only by deposited amounts, decreases only by collected amounts).
After a Collect call, the caller's balance should never increase.

After Collect, the caller's balance is unchanged from before any operations when Collect fails (e.g., due to insufficient balance or MinSum), but the reference ensures this by checking the condition requiring both balances[msg.sender] >= MinSum and balances[msg.sender] >= _am.
After a Collect(0) call from any address, the caller-specific getter c.balances(address) returns exactly the same value as before the deposit-then-collect sequence.
After a Collect call, MinSum must equal the value set by SetMinSum when called before initialization.
After a Collect call, MinSum must equal the _val parameter of the most recent SetMinSum call.
After a successful Collect call, the MinSum value must be less than or equal to the total balance of the caller before the call.
After Collect is called, the MinSum state variable must be equal to the value set by the last SetMinSum call before initialization.
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable must equal the value set by SetMinSum if it was called before initialization, otherwise it must equal the default value 0.
After collecting any amount, the MinSum state variable must still equal its original value set before initialization.
After a Collect call that succeeds (does not revert), the MinSum value must be equal to the value set by SetMinSum before initialization.
After any Collect call that returns successfully (does not revert), MinSum equals the value set during initialization.
For any sequence of operations, after a successful Collect call (non-reverting), MinSum must equal the value set by the last SetMinSum call before initialization, or 0 if never set.
After any sequence of operations ending with a successful Collect call, the MinSum state variable remains equal to its value set by the last SetMinSum call before initialization, or 0 if never set.
Collect does not revert and the balance of the sender remains unchanged if MinSum has not been set (MinSum == 0) and the sender's balance is less than the requested amount.
After calling Collect, MinSum remains unchanged from its initial value (0) regardless of inputs.
After a successful Collect call that does not revert, the sender's balance decreases by exactly the amount collected.
After a Collect call that reverts, MinSum remains unchanged from its initial value (0).
After any call to Collect, MinSum is always equal to its initial value (0).

After any call to Collect with any amount, the MinSum state variable retains its initial value (i.e., the original SetMinSum guarantee that MinSum is only set once before initialization) regardless of the caller and amount.
After any Collect call, MinSum must be the value last set by SetMinSum, not the default zero.
After a call to Collect, MinSum is unchanged from its value before the call (i.e., Collect does not modify MinSum).
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable is unchanged from its value before the call (i.e., Collect does not modify MinSum).
The MinSum value after a call to Collect is either zero (if SetMinSum was never called) or the value set by the most recent call to SetMinSum.
After a call to Collect, the Log state variable is never zero address if Initialized has been called.
After Collect, if the call succeeds and MinSum < balances[msg.sender], the Log state variable is set to the originally provided log file address.
After a call to Collect, if the transaction does not revert and enough time has passed for the log entry to be updated, the LogFile address stored in the contract is always the one that was last set.
After calling Collect, the Log state variable address must never be zero if the call did not revert and Initialized has been called.
After Collect, if Initialized was called and the call does not revert, Log is never the zero address.
After collecting a valid amount, the caller's balance in the contract should decrease by the collected amount, not be set to the collected amount.
After any sequence of operations ending in Collect, the sum of all balances in the contract equals the contract's ether balance, unaffected by the bug.
After calling Collect with a valid amount, the sender's balance in the contract should be equal to their balance before Collect minus the collected amount.
After any call to Collect, the difference between a user's balance and the contract's total balance is invariant.
After any call to Collect, the sum of all user balances in the contract equals the contract's ether balance minus the amount of the last Collect call (which is zero if the call reverted).
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the total of all user balances (sum of balances) plus the contract's own balance is invariant.
When Collect(uint256) returns successfully, the contract's own ETH balance (address(c).balance) must have decreased by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After a successful Collect call, the sum of msg.sender's balance and the contract's ETH balance is preserved if no deposit was zero-valued.

After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), if the caller's balance before Collect was zero, the caller's balance after must remain zero when the original contract allows zero deposits, but the buggy contract reverts such deposits breaking that behavior.

After any call to Collect(uint256), the count of deposits that succeeded (as logged) equals the number of Deposit calls that succeeded (excluding zero-value deposits that revert in the buggy version).
After Collect(uint256), the total of all user balances (obtained by summing c.balances(address)) never exceeds the actual Ether balance of the contract, even after a successful Deposit.
After a successful Collect call, the contract's Ether balance is at least the sum of all user balances.
After Collect, the caller's balance never exceeds their original deposit plus any additional deposit made in the same transaction.
After Collect, the contract's ether balance is exactly equal to the sum of all user balances.
After a call to Collect, the sum of all user balances is never less than the total Ether received by the contract via deposits that are recorded in the balances.
